newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Philippine hopes to buy HK's patrol boats - paper.
newsitem.headline: Philippine hopes to buy HK's patrol boats - paper.

text.p: The Philippines hopes to buy three naval patrol boats as Britain slashes its military presence and sells off Hong Kong military hardware ahead of the colony's 1997 return to China, a newspaper said on Monday.

But a British defence official told Reuters that discussions were continuing, and no deal had yet been completed on the sale of the Peacock, the Plover and the Starling. A number of parties had expressed an interest, the official added.
The South China Morning Post quoted sources as saying the Philippines had offered to buy the three, 62-metre (217-foot) ships, which were acquired in 1981 to patrol Hong Kong waters.
The British colony will return to Chinese control at midnight next June 30, and Beijing will deploy its own defence forces in the territory after the handover.
The vessels were priced at HK$151 million each in 1981. Two sister ships fetched $53 million when they were sold in 1988.
